notes: Act 110 of 2026 (H.4216) rewrote South Carolina's income tax starting with tax year 2026: two brackets (1.99% on taxable income under $30,000; 5.21% minus $966 at $30,000 and above, i.e. 5.21% marginal above $30,000), one schedule for all filing statuses. SCDOR Information Letter #26-20 confirms the 2026 figures. Brackets are indexed in later years.

Starting in 2026, South Carolina begins with federal AGI (not federal taxable income) and does not allow the federal standard/itemized deductions or the federal QBI, tips, overtime, car-loan-interest or senior deductions.

The South Carolina Income Adjusted Deduction (SCIAD) shown as the standard deduction ($15,000 single/MFS, $22,500 HoH, $30,000 MFJ) phases out in proportion to federal AGI: single from $40,000 to $95,000, HoH from $60,000 to $142,500, MFJ from $80,000 to $190,000. Modeled.

Optional 3% flat rate on active trade or business income (SC Code § 12-6-545, Form I-335) is available to sole proprietors, but income reasonably related to the owner's personal services is excluded, so it usually helps freelancers little; not modeled.
Top-rate reductions under Act 110 can start no earlier than tax year 2027. Dependent exemption, retirement-income and age-65 deductions, the $200-capped SC EITC and other credits are not modeled.

seDeduction.note: South Carolina now starts from federal AGI, so the deductible half of SE tax carries through.

seHealthInsurance.note: The federal self-employed health insurance deduction is part of federal AGI and carries through.

retirementContributions.note: SEP-IRA and solo 401(k) contributions deducted for federal AGI carry through to South Carolina.

qbi.note: Act 110 decouples South Carolina from IRC § 63(b)-(g), so the federal QBI deduction is not allowed starting in 2026.

localIncomeTax.note: South Carolina counties and cities do not levy a local income tax.

estimatedTax.threshold: Required if you expect to owe $100 or more with your SC1040 after withholding and credits.
estimatedTax.safeHarbor: Generally no penalty if timely estimates equal 100% of the prior-year SC tax (110% if prior-year AGI exceeded $150,000), or if you pay at least 90% of the current-year tax. SCDOR Information Letter #26-20 explains adjusting 2026 payments for Act 110.

businessCosts.llcFormationFee: $110 Articles of Organization (South Carolina Secretary of State, S.C. Code § 33-44-1204).
businessCosts.annualReportFee: None. An LLC not taxed as a corporation files no annual report and pays no corporate license fee.
businessCosts.franchiseOrMinimumTax: None for sole proprietors or LLCs taxed as sole proprietorships/partnerships (the corporate license fee applies only to LLCs taxed as corporations).
businessCosts.grossReceiptsTax: None at the state level. Check your city or county for any local business license requirement.
